hints: Focus on the shape around each central atom, since bond angle is decided by electron-pair repulsion and VSEPR theory.
Work out the number of bonding pairs and lone pairs on carbon in $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$, on nitrogen in $\text{NH}_4^+$ and on nitrogen in $\text{NH}_3$.
Remember that a lone pair repels more strongly than bonding pairs, so it squeezes the bond angle down below the perfect tetrahedral angle.
walkthrough:
**Recall how shape controls bond angle**

Think of electron pairs spreading out as far as possible. More repulsion means a smaller squeeze on the bonds.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{lone pair-lone pair > lone pair-bond pair > bond pair-bond pair}$$

**Assign the shape of each species**

In $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ each carbon has 3 bonding regions and no lone pairs, so trigonal planar with angle about $120^{\circ}$. In $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ the $\text{C=O}$ carbon is also trigonal planar, about $120^{\circ}$, and the methyl carbons are tetrahedral, about $109.5^{\circ}$.

For nitrogen species:
$$\text{NH}_4^+ : 4 \text{ bond pairs, 0 lone pairs} \rightarrow \text{tetrahedral, } 109.5^{\circ}$$
$$\text{NH}_3 : 3 \text{ bond pairs, 1 lone pair} \rightarrow \text{trigonal pyramidal, } \sim 107^{\circ}$$

**Compare and pick the smallest**

The largest angles are near $120^{\circ}$, then $109.5^{\circ}$, then the lone-pair-squeezed angle near $107^{\circ}$. That smallest value belongs to ammonia with its one active lone pair.

options.A: Incorrect. In $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ each carbon is trigonal planar with H-C-H and H-C-C angles of about $120^{\circ}$. This is larger than tetrahedral and pyramidal angles, so it cannot be the smallest.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ contains trigonal planar centres (about $120^{\circ}$) at the carbonyl carbon and tetrahedral centres (about $109.5^{\circ}$) at the methyl carbons. Both are larger than the lone-pair-squeezed angle in ammonia.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{NH}_4^+$ has four identical N-H bonding pairs and no lone pair, giving a perfect tetrahedral angle of $109.5^{\circ}$. Students often confuse it with $\text{NH}_3$, but losing the lone pair to form the fourth bond removes the extra squeezing effect.
options.D: Correct. $\text{NH}_3$ has 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair on nitrogen, giving a trigonal pyramidal shape. The lone pair repels strongly and squeezes the H-N-H angle down to about $107^{\circ}$, the smallest of the four.
